newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian heart surgeon says Yeltsin "satisfactory".
newsitem.headline: Russian heart surgeon says Yeltsin "satisfactory".

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, who was admitted to hospital on Wednesday evening with early signs of pneumonia, is in "quite satisfactory" condition, his heart surgeon said on Thursday.
Renat Akchurin, who led the heart surgery on Yeltsin last November, told reporters he had not seen the president himself but had spoken to doctors treating him.
"As far as I know, Yeltsin's health is quite satisfactory, and he is receiving regular medication," said Akchurin. "It's true that I haven't seen him, but I know this from his physicians."
The Kremlin announced on Monday that Yeltsin had a heavy cold, just two weeks after his return to work following the heart surgery on November 5.
But on Wednesday evening officials said Yeltsin had gone to the Central Clinical Hospital in Moscow for better treatment and diagnosis of early signs of pneumonia.

Akchurin said Yeltsin's latest illness was an "ordinary flu" unrelated to his heart operation. Such a flu, common in Russia at this time of the year, is easily passed from one member of the family to the other, he said.
"The post-operative period finished already a month ago, so it seems to me that it makes no sense to connect something with the operation now," he said.
He also said that Yeltsin's overall health allowed him to perform his responsibilities as president.
"He is a completely normal and capable person; what's all this talk about? It's pure political speculation, I'm absolutely convinced of this," the heart surgeon said.

Yeltsin's latest bout of bad health has again raised concern about his ability to lead the country as the Kremlin has a long tradition of attempting to hide major illnesses under the mask of a cold and the flu.
